title: Automation affordances for tests: a field selector on ui-state and wait-for-state-condition
description:
UI flows are driven by pixel coordinates (UI-9 and ENG-29 made 15 `click --x 512 --y 565`-style clicks each) and polled by hand; ui-state dumps the whole snapshot so agents pipe it to python3 -c to pick fields (30 times). Evidence: ai-workspace reports/tool-review-2026-10-18.md items 8 and 10. Add: click by label (a menu item, control row or text element's text, resolved from the scene's own state), ui-state --field <dotted path> (repeatable), and a wait route/CLI flag that waits until a state predicate holds (with a timeout) instead of sleeps. Build these on the per-scene state export of IX-5, so scene UI changes do not require changing these routes.

Click by label was split out to TOOL-37 (user, 2026-10-21): it reads the drawn HyperStrings and needs no scene state, so it is not blocked by IX-5. This ticket keeps --field and the wait route.
definition-of-done:
1. ixdar-cli ui-state --field a.b (repeatable) prints just those values.
2. ixdar-cli wait --until '<field> == <value>' --timeout N returns when it holds, or fails with the last value at the timeout.
3. Both read the IX-5 state export, not per-scene code.
testing-plan: 1. Drive the main menu and the knot editor by label; wait on activeTool; paste outputs.
